preservation_certificate.proof_artifact: PROOF_MAP.md and lean/H116FiberTrace.lean; a full finite certificate and an eleven-coefficient quotient/ten-coefficient curve-identity certificate each imply the recurrence. The Lean cutoff proves X^(p-1) is invisible below degree 22 for prime p>19. Against Mathlib's actual FormalGroup, Lean now proves Y divides F(X,Y)-X, an X^m correction preserves the prefix below m, and the leading-X double-pole bridge loses exactly one degree. The generic prefix-transfer lemmas preserve unit inverse squares and a regular outer unit; PREFIX_TRANSFER_EXPERIMENT.md measures that the pole loss is sharp in 20 finite-field controls and REGULAR_SUBSTITUTION_EXPERIMENT.md verifies all three composition boundaries in 20 further cases. The curve-coordinate instance identifies the outer unit by q=1+A X^4q^2+B X^6q^3, proves the cleared affine identity, target rescaling and complete normalized x-ratio prefix; CURVE_COORDINATE_EXPERIMENT.md checks the corresponding 24-coefficient formulas on five curves and identity certificate IDC1h692b3e04c6a4f0cd seals the rescaling polynomial. The additive-endomorphism specialization derives V+pi=[t] from pointwise injectivity, pi*V=[p], and the characteristic equation; a ZMod 2 mutation proves injectivity is a necessary boundary. The affine-point instance constructs pi from Mathlib's finite-field Frobenius, inherits additivity and injectivity, and proves the exact (x^p,y^p) coordinate action over ZMod p. Over algebraic extensions the inverse Frobenius point map now defines V=[p]*piInverse and proves pi*V=[p]; Lean rearranges the resulting sum identity to V-1=[t-1]-pi, proves equality after the actual affine-point observable z=-x/y, and supplies a generating-set certificate interface with trace fixed to p+1-Nat.card E(F_p). It also proves that every algebraic affine point lies in a positive Frobenius-fixed locus and that characteristic checks on every such locus imply the global pointwise V-1 identity; a ZMod 3 control shows one locus is insufficient. Lean additionally proves that sufficiently many pole-free finite evaluations separate supplied rational functions below a strict cross-product degree bound, with a formal strictness control. After the retained split-pole failure, Lean proves that V-fixed points have Frobenius eigenvalue t-1, iterates that relation, and identifies their Frobenius fixed-locus condition with the scalar condition. It proves the exact norm factor (V-1)(pi-1)=[p+1-t] and packages the remaining degree step: degree multiplicativity, deg[N]=N^2 and equal degrees for the dual pair imply deg(V-1)=N; a 4*9=6^2 control proves the equal-degree premise is necessary. It now proves finite field-tower degree multiplication and the equal-adjacent-degree consequence, and exposes Mathlib's exact (N^2,N^2-1) division-polynomial coordinate degrees under the nonzero-characteristic premise; SCALAR_DIVPOLY_DEGREE_EXPERIMENT.md independently checks these coordinates and the excluded [p] degree collapse. POINTWISE_RATIONAL_RECONSTRUCTION_V2_EXPERIMENT.md jointly reconstructs three stable full base-field rational candidates with strict separation margins, and KERNEL_X_ORBIT_EXPERIMENT.md verifies that their denominator roots follow the plus/minus Frobenius eigenspace union modulo sign. Generic pullback construction, coordinate-to-morphism degree, dual-isogeny, cyclicity and scheme/local-series identification remain explicit. The restricted characteristic family remains explicit. FROBENIUS_BOUNDARY_EXPERIMENT.md records the preregistered p=31 first difference 15 and delta 10 with two map identities and three rejected controls. MAP_CERTIFICATE_EXPERIMENT.md, JET_CERTIFICATE_EXPERIMENT.md, FORMAL_SCALAR_JET_EXPERIMENT.md and FORMAL_SCALAR_OOS_EXPERIMENT.md record independently replayed excluded-map controls
